public_rationale: FaithBench documents hallucinations in contemporary models, including a concrete GPT-4o fabrication. That settles the firm claim that hallucinations had not vanished. Marcus's concession that they may have declined requires no separate trend finding.
limitations: The benchmark deliberately selects challenging summaries.
Source faithfulness and factual correctness are different concepts; the cited example invents an unsupported relationship.
The source identifies the evaluation year but not an exact execution date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM hallucinations may have declined but have not vanished.

statement.excerpt: They may have declined, but they certainly haven’t vanished.

our_interpretation: May have declined concedes possible improvement; it does not assert a measured downward trend.
The firm commitment is that hallucinations remained present in contemporary LLMs.
I use 2024 through publication, following the surrounding reference to the latest 2024 edition. Model evaluations have no standard reporting quarter.
criteria.support_condition: A reproducible contemporary evaluation documents genuine hallucinations in an LLM within the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that contemporary LLMs had eliminated hallucinations across their relevant factual uses.
